title: Rollforward sandglass checklist and shift roster — Nov 2027 (draft)
body:
Context:
This is a compact field notebook for the Nov 2027 rollforward using the 'sandglass' phasing pattern — small, accelerating traffic windows that let us validate latencies, cache behavior, and model quality as we move from canary to full capacity. Draft/working doc: expects edits from SRE, Serving Runtime, and Product Ops.

Goals:
- Validate model routing and fallback behavior across Dedicated and Hosted API zones.
- Confirm prefix/KV cache warm-up curves and hit-rate inflection points.
- Keep tail latency within the SLO band (p95 < 350ms for short seq workloads, < 600ms for long seq).
- Avoid global fails by graceful degradation (fallback model or regional reroute).

High-level plan (sandglass windows):
- Day 0 (preflight): infra smoke, canary model pinned, key monitors active.
- Day 1 (micro-window): 0.5% traffic for 15 minutes -> observe cache, p50/p95, error budget usage.
- Day 1 (pulse): 2% for 45 minutes -> check steady-state, KV warming, batching efficiency.
- Day 2 (ramp): 10% for 2 hours with routing weight changes every 30m (0.5x -> 1x -> 2x).
- Day 3 (validation): 35% for 4 hours; run QA prompt set and reranking spot checks.
- Day 4 (cut-over): 100% progressive in region groups, maintain safety-lane.

Preflight checklist (owner: Aisha / Eng oncall):
- [ ] Confirm release artifacts: model tarball hash, quantization profile, config commit (review PR #789).
- [ ] Backfill release notes in console and customer-facing changelog draft.
- [ ] Confirm Dedicated pool reserved capacity and burst policy (capacity: 120 GPUs).
- [ ] Create canary routing rule (pin to control plane v2) and model-variant fallback mapping.
- [ ] Ensure KMS keys available for private deployments; validate HSM integration smoke.
- [ ] Schedule SLO burn watch: channels, paging lists, primary/secondary responders.
- [ ] Prepare QA prompt set (10 prompts per vertical) and automated eval harness.
- [ ] Telemetry queries saved and exported to shared dashboard (see telemetry queries below).

Shift roster (operational windows) — Nov 2027 rollforward:
- Day 0: Aisha (lead), Julian (SRE), Kenji (Serving), Priya (Product Ops) — 09:00–18:00 PT
- Day 1: Julian (lead), Kenji (serving oncall), Maya (observability), Aisha (backup) — 06:00–14:00 PT
- Day 2: Kenji (lead), Priya (QA), Alex (network), Julian (backup) — 12:00–20:00 PT
- Day 3: Priya (lead), Aisha (observability), Kenji (serving), Julian (release engineer) — 08:00–16:00 PT
- Nightwatch (overnight): oncall rotation active; escalation to SRE L2 after 2 pager cycles.

Operational play snippets:
- Quick rollback command (control plane): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/releases/rollback -d '{"release_id":"release-20271101","target_variant":"previous"}'
- Canary weight adjust: rdctl routing set-weight --route model-inference --variant canary=0.02 --variant stable=0.98
- Cache flush (targeted): rdctl cache purge --scope pooled-prefix --model-id rwd-llm-1 --node-group eu-west-1

Telemetry queries (save exact dashboard names):
- inference_latency_p50_p95_by_model (group by model_variant, region)
- errors_5xx_rate (alert if >0.2% sustained over 5m)
- queue_depth_by_instance (alert if >120 for >3m)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (critical threshold: >70% after 30m warmup)
- batching_efficiency_tokens_per_batch (expect 8–16 tokens/batch for short seq flows)

Bailout/rollback triggers (immediate pause and investigate):
- sustained p95 > 3x baseline for >10m across >2 regions -> pause ramp and rollback to previous variant.
- error rate > 1% or sustained increase >5x normal -> pause, point-in-time rollout revert.
- cache_hit_rate below 30% after 45m of load -> pause and run cache diagnostic.
- missing telemetry (dashboards reporting stale data) -> consider abort, route to fallback.

Gradual mitigation steps (if a trigger fires):
1) Pause traffic ramp, set routing weight to stable=100% (rdctl routing set-weight ...).
2) If errors persist, invoke rollback API to previous release artifact.
3) Postmortem snapshot: collect heap dumps, kernel logs, model server traces, and recent request samples (store in /var/release-artifacts/rollforward-2027-11).

QA & quality checks during windows:
- Run the 40-item QA prompt set (automated) every window start and end; compare token-level diffs and quality score drift.
- Human spot-check: sampling 20 responses across verticals (search snippets, completion coherency, hallucination checks).
- Evaluate latency tail and token cost delta; log per-request token counts to billing sampler.

Communication plan:
- Slack channel: #releases-rollforward (pin timeline and runbook refs).
- Email blast to internal stakeholders after Day 2 validation (template in Confluence link).
- External customer note: only if rollback or user-visible changes — product to approve copy.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Is the Dedicated burst policy sufficient for global test traffic? (Kenji to validate with capacity sim by 2027-11-03).
- Confirm whether the HSM rotation will impact key fetch latency in private clusters — Priya to prod-test.
- Need an extra observer for EU region during Day 3 ramp (ask Maya or add contractor).

Post-rollforward checklist (first 72h):
- [ ] Run regression eval suite across historical prompt sets.
- [ ] Check billing sampler for token cost anomalies.
- [ ] Archive temporary debug artifacts and mark them in the release ticket.
- [ ] Draft post-rollforward debrief and action items (owner: Aisha)

Notes (informal):
- Keep an eye on model routing fallbacks — last time we saw a subtle config drift at 8% weight change that dropped cache hit-rate. Sandglass windows should catch that early.
- If paging becomes noisy, escalate to strategy: increase sampling frequency but reduce alert volume (mute not helpful).
- "Notes to self": make the QA harness output include a short-readability score next time.

Attachments/links embedded:
- QA harness script: /repo/release/scripts/qa_harness_run.sh
- Telemetry dashboard: Releases / Sandglass Rollforward 2027-11
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/789

Revision history:
- 2027-11-02: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2027-11-03: added telemetry queries and bailouts (Julian)
- 2027-11-04: shift roster tightened; added QA checklist (Kenji)

End of doc.
